source_text: Nunc vero si colligam, quae sunt in Evangelio abusive prolata, non sustinent; multo magis apostolus Paulus nullam errori occasionem praebuit, qui nihil dixit improprium, si pronuntiavit, peccatorem primum hominem sequentibus peccantibus exemplum fuisse.
pass_a_gloss: But now if I collect those things which have been brought forth abusively in the Gospel, they do not support them; much more the apostle Paul offered no occasion to error, who said nothing improper, if he pronounced that the first sinning human being was an example to those sinning afterward.

lemmas.lexica: LS exemplum; Blaise Adam as example not transmitter
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: But as things stand, even if I gather the Gospel’s figurative expressions, they do not support them. Much less did the apostle Paul provide any occasion for error: he said nothing improper if he declared that the first sinful man was an example to later sinners (compare Romans 5:12) (Romans 5:12).

choices.why: Adam as example to later sinners, Julian's alternative to tradux.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: The Latin phrase “non sustinent” has an unstated object; the sense is that even the Gospel’s figurative expressions do not support the opposing interpretation.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
